# Case study: is height hereditary?

```{r}
library(dslabs)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(HistData)
data("GaltonFamilies")
```

```{r}
set.seed(1983)
galton <- as.data.frame(GaltonFamilies)

galton_sample <- GaltonFamilies |>
  filter(gender == "male") |>
  group_by(family) |>
  # Get a single, randomly selected male child
  slice_sample(n = 1) |> 
  ungroup() |>
  select(
    father,
    # rename to son
    son = childHeight 
  )
```

We can compute summary stats for this dataset:
```{r}
galton_sample |>
  summarise(
    mean_father = mean(father),
    sd_father   = sd(father),
    mean_son    = mean(son),
    sd_son      = sd(son)
  )
```

(I'm going to be more picky about this and force the x and y axis coordinates to be the same)
```{r}
galton_sample |> ggplot(aes(father, son)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(60, 80), ylim = c(60, 80), ratio = 1) + 
  theme_bw()
```

# The correlation coefficient

```{r}
with(galton_sample, cor(father, son))
```

## Sample correlation is a random variable

```{r}
r <- galton_sample |>
  slice_sample(n = 25, replace = TRUE) |>
  summarise(r = cor(father, son)) |>
  pull(r)

r
```

```{r}
library(infer)
r <- galton_sample |>
  rep_slice_sample(reps = 1000, n = 25, replace = TRUE) |>
  summarise(r = cor(father, son))
```

```{r}
ggplot(r, aes(x = r)) + geom_histogram(color = "black", fill = "grey") + theme_bw()
```

```{r}
mean(r$r)
sd(r$r)
```


```{r}
library(qqplotr) # Makes nicer qq plots (imo)
ggplot(data = r, aes(sample = r)) + 
  stat_qq_point() + 
  stat_qq_line() + 
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_bw() + ylab("Sample Quantile") + xlab("Theoretical Quantile")
```

```{r}
ggplot(data = r, aes(sample = r)) + 
  stat_qq_band() + 
  stat_qq_line() +
  stat_qq_point(bandtype = "ts", conf = .95) + 
  theme_bw() + ylab("Sample Quantile") + xlab("Theoretical Quantile")
```


```{r}
r40 <- galton_sample |>
  rep_slice_sample(reps = 1000, n = 40, replace = TRUE) |>
  summarise(r = cor(father, son))

ggplot(data = r40, aes(sample = r)) + 
  stat_qq_band() +

r50 <- galton_sample |>
  rep_slice_sample(reps = 1000, n = 50, replace = TRUE) |>
  summarise(r = cor(father, son))

ggplot(data = r50, aes(sample = r)) +

```

# The regression line

```{r}
fit <- lm(son ~ father, data = galton_sample)
summary(fit)

print(coef(fit))

params <- coef(fit) # get slope and intercept from lm directly
```


```{r}
ggplot(galton_sample, aes(x = father, y = son)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  # blue line
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  # black line
  geom_abline(slope = params[2], intercept =  params[1]) +
  labs(title = "Regression Line") + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(60, 80), ylim = c(60, 80), ratio = 1) + 
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
ggplot(galton_sample, aes(x = scale(father), y = scale(son))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Regression Line, Standardized Units") +  
  coord_fixed() + 
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
# Variance explained (R-squared)
print(summary(fit)$r.squared)

```

## Linear regression improves precision

```{r}
B <- 1000
N <- 50


results <- galton_sample |>
  rep_slice_sample(reps = B, n = N, replace = TRUE) |>
  summarise(
    # Conditional average with stratification
    ca = mean(son[round(father)==72]), 
    # Linear regression prediction
    lm = predict(lm(son ~ father), newdata = data.frame(father = 72)))

sd(results$ca, na.rm = T)
sd(results$lm, na.rm = T)
```


## Bivariate normal distribution justification

```{r}
galton_sample |>
  mutate(father_z = (father-mean(father))/sd(father), 
         father_z_round = round(father_z), 
         son_z = (son - mean(son))/sd(son)) |>
  # Remove outliers
  filter(father_z_round <=2, father_z_round >= -2) |> 
  ggplot() + stat_qq(aes(sample = son_z)) + 
  facet_wrap(~father_z_round, ncol = 5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1) + 
  coord_fixed() + 
  theme_bw()

```
